# Results

The 7 November exceptional-sign continuation gives 352832 in 32D (+32 over the reviewed repository certificate and +512 over the pinned Lin result). All 352832 integer vectors are reconstructed; three exact verification routes cover every pair category, including 1383616 direct exceptional pairs. The same 25 exceptional supports attain their exact limited-source capacity of 1664. No global optimality or worldwide-priority claim is made. Historical certificates and the manuscript are unchanged.

The 6 November rational heavy-head rotation gives 390992 in 34D (+2 over the preceding 390990 certificate). A changed dense coordinate placement and star parity permit shared root deletion and restore two roots. Two independent exact proofs check all finite layers, uniqueness and rank 34; common scaling gives squared integer norm 5780000 and product bound 2890000. Historical constructions and the manuscript are unchanged.

The 7 November pruned 29-orbit continuation gives 769852 in 39D (+32 over the preceding published 769820 certificate). It combines all 441244 retained sparse points with 10269 sign orbits of order 32. Two independent exact proofs check all 1687391811 relative products and the actual middle-support geometry, with four extrema-witness replays and eight new geometric rejection controls. All previous published certificates and the manuscript are retained unchanged.

The 29 October continuation gives 209807, 221988, 231697, 247972, 251188 in 27-31D, exceeding PackingStar commit 477df34 by 47, 124, 21, 5, 19 points. Corrected sextet symmetries reclaim 28D and further strengthen 27D, 29D and 31D. Complete exact coordinate replays and independent direct-int64 insertion checks pass. The manuscript remains deferred.

The historical synchronized 28 October registry included 201136, 209600, 221694, 231638, 247960 and 251110 in dimensions 26-31, gains of 2, 14, 30, 2, 4 and 108 over PackingStar commit b67832a. Complete coordinate replays verify the integer and quadratic configurations, including all unpaired points. The concurrent 33-96D improvements and corrected nonlinear-code comparisons are retained; the paper remains deferred.

The further 28 October continuation gives 370376 in 33D (+8), 390990 in 34D (+8), 415334 in 35D (+20), 501687 in 36D (+15) and 505503 in 37D (+15), compared with the preceding repository certificates. Shared root-star deletions and a latitude-preserving phase refill have two independent exact proof routes, reconstruction and rejection controls. Broader complete-support, signed-region and base-choice searches have not yielded a larger verified gain in this pass. The 32D, 38D and 39D bounds are unchanged.

The 6 November orthogonal Hamming construction gives 611638 in 38D (+116 over the preceding 611522-point repository certificate). It replaces 384 cube-edge points by 512 Hamming points, restores four cap lines and removes six new lines, for 12 additional cap deletions. Two exact proof routes check the new layer and retained components; the cap-cap bound inherits the source Golay/Leech minimum-norm argument rather than an exhaustive Leech-pair enumeration. Full seven-coordinate heads and a new norm split escape the old 63-support ceiling. The manuscript remains deferred.

The 6 November antipodal-direction completion gives 58,543,525 in 60D (+575,182 over the preceding repository construction). A known antipodal 840-point quaternionic code supplies 420 direction pairs instead of 378; the 841-point pole code is independent. Joint selection and reassignment of complete classes adds a further 704 points over the first 58,542,821-point composition. Exact tail, pole, base-class, isometry and full-coordinate disjointness checks pass. The published P48 minimum and mother-shell population remain explicit inputs. The manuscript is unchanged.

The 4 November algebraic completion gives 209825 in 27D (+18) and 251196 in 31D (+8). Individual signed-support choices share 14 deletions for 32 additions in 27D. An eight-point orthogonal sign cube fills a 31D hole without deletion. Both complete explicit configurations and all changed pairs replay exactly; the registered engine reproduces the selections. The manuscript is unchanged.

The 6 November medium-body splitting continuation gives 2,919,803 points (+4 over the retained 2,919,799-point Weyl construction). Six medium points and three tiny points are removed; twelve medium points and one tiny point are inserted. Two exact implementations pass 431,912 changed-interaction checks, with fresh geometry/gluing and medium-membership checks. P48n minimum/design and family completeness/populations remain inherited; no full large-shell enumeration or worldwide-priority assertion is made. The manuscript remains unchanged.
The 4 November finite body/head 43D continuation gives 2919785 points (+3 over the preceding 2919782 certificate), with 3450 explicit tiny points. The generic engine independently generated the same final point set as the separate discovery task. Both ambient and coefficient-coordinate exact replays pass. Complete-family population inputs and the deferred manuscript scope are unchanged.

The 7 November Coxeter-Todd triangle-switch continuation gives 501813 in 36D and 505629 in 37D, adding 126 to each preceding certificate. Ninety independent three-point base switches combine with 1511 added and 1469 removed equatorial phase orbits. Two exact coordinate proofs replay every affected category, including new equator versus unchanged base, and retain all 636 lift-body orbits at both heights. The original source and manuscript remain unchanged.

The 28 October Coxeter-Todd continuation gives 501672 in 36D (+39) and 505488 in 37D (+129), with two independent exact representations and reproducible phase trades.

The 28 October nonlinear-code correction and section construction raises every bound in 88–96D, from 6,921,251,584 in 88D to 142,162,362,560 in 96D. The parent (96,2^37,24) binary code is published work of Duursma–Greferath–Litsyn–Schmidt (2001), previously missed by this repository's linear-code comparison. Its shortenings correct the comparison floors in 92–96D. Two independent finite proofs recheck all 16,777,216 Z4 words, 4,166,151 octad-coset exclusions and 338,559,231 support pairs. The 96D result exceeds the derived standard chain with that parent by 426,344,448 points. The manuscript remains deferred.

The 28 October dual-obstruction continuation gives 7,101,541,132 in 95D (+9,209,856) and 13,313,343,680 in 96D (+22,560,768). Its 26,022-support certificate checks all 338,559,231 distinct pairs in two exact representations. Disjoint odd GF(4) trace checks prove compatibility for 2,073 supports in thirteen or fourteen rows, extending the former twelve-row restriction. The manuscript remains deferred.

The further 28 October continuation gives 6,218,206,932 in 73D from 7,663 explicit norm-ten heads; signed-tail orbit proofs give 6,220,170,666 in 82D, 6,221,008,658 in 83D, 6,222,025,404 in 84D, 6,223,222,688 in 85D and 6,226,194,610 in 87D. A 24,645-support certificate gives 7,092,331,276 in 95D and 13,290,782,912 in 96D. The new explicit layer checks 120,048,558 products in two exact arithmetics, the signed profiles have an independent polynomial replay, and both support representations check all 303,675,690 pairs. The manuscript remains deferred.

The 28 October mixed-tail weighted-priority continuation gives 6,218,490,542 in 77D, 6,218,688,770 in 78D and 6,218,922,650 in 79D, improving the preceding certificates by 25,526, 2,890 and 10,614 points. All 22,848,388 ordered tail products, joint tail/pole ranks and rational expectations are checked exactly. These are existence proofs under the stated Gamma72/design inputs; selected head sets are not enumerated. The manuscript retains its earlier snapshot.

The 28 October fill/correct continuation gives 13290553536 in 96D (+294912 over the preceding registered bound) and 7092187916 in 95D (+180224), with all 303330765 support pairs checked in two independent representations. PackingStar reports larger 26–31D bounds; README.md records these supersessions from the pinned 28 October source review. The paper retains its earlier values. The later 26 October update adds 352800 in 32D, 370368 in 33D, 390982 in 34D and 415314 in 35D, each with two independent exact proof representations. The paper update is deferred; common/manuscript_scope.json records its 66-result state and hashes. The 26 October continuation gives 197584 in 25D, 241742 in 31D, 610394 in 38D, 769180 in 39D and 1126314 in the newly registered dimension 40. All five independent exact replays passed. Fresh primary-source comparisons and the unavailable Cohn retrieval are documented in common/source_review_20261026.json. The 24 October 2026 checkpoint adds exact Coxeter-Todd constructions in dimensions 36 and 37, registers the supplied 2 919 743-point partial-family 43D certificate, and raises 45D to 7 655 056. All 41-46D integer angles and head dimensions replay; complete-family body populations inherit the documented identities and have not all been freshly enumerated. The 25 October continuation adds shared midpoint replacements with 200,918 points in 26D and 204,636 in 27D, adds 216,568 points in 29D and 224,280 in 30D, regains 38D with 605,346 and 39D with 768,924, and strengthens 73D and 76-96D. The norm-ten continuation gives 6,218,204,076 in 73D and exact finite-graph existence bounds in 77-79D. The checkpoint also includes the 205,232-point joint Leech lift in 28D, the 7 387-line P48 class family, code constructions in 61-68D and 95-96D, including the new signed-support 64-65D constructions, and Gamma72 nearest-coset lifts. The comparison column uses common/published.py's pinned published data; this integration is not a new comprehensive literature audit. The paper currently reports the preceding 66-result checkpoint; the four new 32-35D results await a later manuscript update. Its September appendix is retained. See [verification scope](verifications/improved/dim41-46-p48-heads/README.md).

# Kissing numbers: constructions and verification in dimensions 18 through 96

The kissing number τ(n) is the largest number of unit spheres that can touch a central unit
sphere in ℝⁿ; equivalently, the largest set of unit vectors with pairwise inner products at
most 1/2. This repository registers constructions in **70 dimensions**, each with a package
that states its verification scope, together with the negative results that guide further
searches. Some of our earlier records have since been superseded. Their constructions,
values and verification packages remain here as part of the research record.

> [!IMPORTANT]

The new 27D and 31D certificates check every pair in complete explicit integer
coordinates, with separate direct-integer checks of all changed pairs. They
assume no lattice minimum or unenumerated population. The 43D proof has the
inherited-input scope stated above. These are verified lower bounds; the


`update.py` is the maintainer's entry point rather than the reviewer's: it runs every package
driver, then `audit.py`, then `audit.py --write-results`, then each package's table generator,
then the paper's tables and its checkers, then `run_all.py` -- in that order, so a number can

## The construction ideas

**Coxeter–Todd phase codes (36–37).** Three rank-12 blocks carry a fixed
403 704-point base and 32 661 selected three-point phase orbits. Exact shell
enumeration and integer angles prove squared distance at least 12. Two latitude
layers add 3 816 points in 37D. The earlier full-cell and phase constructions are retained
in the package history; the new latitude layer uses partial three-point orbits.

**Independently normalized body families and heads (41–46).** The October constructions
use a rank-40 complement of sqrt(3) E8 in P48n, with heads in one to six dimensions.
Each family is normalized separately, so families can have different original lengths.
Joint class replacements and head motions admit additional complete or partial families;
zero-body points in the existing head span give the latest 41D, 42D, 45D and 46D
extensions. The supplied 43D construction replaces its tiny layer with 3 447 explicit
body/head pairs, while coordinated 45D motion admits further complete families.
Exact checks, population assumptions and fresh
replay reports are documented in the
[verification package](verifications/improved/dim41-46-p48-heads/).

**Cross-sections of extremal lattices (46, 47, 68–71).** For an extremal even unimodular
lattice, Venkov's theorem makes the minimal shell a spherical 11-design, so every polynomial
of degree ≤ 11 integrates exactly. Applied to *products* of inner products with several fixed
minimal vectors this constrains the **k-point** distribution, and minimising the all-zero
cell by linear programming — with an exact rational dual certificate, plus translation and
lattice-range constraints that the design property cannot see — bounds the cross-section.
Dimension 46 comes out **exact** (the LP minimum and maximum coincide). The same code
reproduces every cross-section whose answer is known: E₇ = 126, Λ₂₃ = 93 150, D₆ = 60,
E₆ = 72, 43 164, 44 550, 49 896, 27 720. Mathematics in
`[common/PROOF-kpoint.md](common/PROOF-kpoint.md)`.

**The cap construction (25–27–31, 38, 49–63, 73–95).** In ℝⁿ ⊕ ℝᵏ, put a lattice shell on the
equator, delete a few lines, and put "caps" above the deleted directions. The optimum uses
**zero-sum triples** of cap directions rather than antipodal pairs, which needs class
threshold γ ≤ 1/4 and cap level t = 2/3; three is the maximum possible, because *n* points
pairwise at cosine ≤ −1/2 force *n* ≤ 3. Run over the Leech with its 248-line class this
reproduces Cohn's table in dimensions 26, 28, 29, 30, 31 **exactly** and beats it in 25 and
27 — a strong check on the model, and it is run as such by
`[verifications/improved/dim73-95-gamma72-caps/scripts/calibrate.py](verifications/improved/dim73-95-gamma72-caps/scripts/calibrate.py)`.

**Axis-layer comparison.** In the retained 73–95D cap construction, the shell rule
became the search space, and cost 221 025 spheres relative to the shipped
rotated and record axis layers (229 743 rather than 8 718 points across the
23 layers). This is a comparison within that construction, not an additional
gain to add to the current record table; `audit.py` recomputes it from the files.

**Explicit classes.** The gain is proportional to the size of a *class* — a set of lines with
pairwise |⟨u,u′⟩| ≤ μ/4 for Γ₇₂ and ≤ μ/3 for P₄₈. Caro–Wei bounds it with no coordinates at all, but real search does
about ten times better in every lattice tried: 221 → **2118** for Γ₇₂, 712 → **7783** for
P₄₈, and 32 000 pairwise-disjoint classes totalling 47 150 230 lines.

**The Edel–Rains–Sloane chain, evaluated where its authors did not (39, 62, 63).** Their count
is a sum over a chain of support sizes, `N(n) = Σ_ν A(n, n_ν, n_ν)·A(n_ν, ⌈n_ν/4⌉)`, and they
evaluated it only at 32, 36, 40, 44, 64, 80 and 128. At `n = 39` with the 2026 constant-weight
tables it gives 756 116; at `n = 62` and `n = 63` the chain `(n, 15, 2)` gives 71 310 732 and
138 419 844. Its levels above zero are **built** here rather than cited — a cyclic `[15,6,8]₄`
through the grid map, and a `[15,10,4]` — and the whole chain is checked in coordinates at
`n = 8` and `n = 16`, where it reproduces τ(8) = 240 (the E₈ root system) and τ(16) = 4320 (the
Barnes–Wall value, and the record) exactly.

## Standards

**Two suites exist specifically to attack the mathematics rather than the bookkeeping**, and
they are the ones to run if you doubt any of this:

```bash
python common/validate_lp.py    # 15 independently known truths, each inside its LP bracket
python common/capalgebra.py     # the cap construction's algebra and count, from scratch
```

`validate_lp.py` exists because the k-point LP produces *lower* bounds: one that is too small
is merely weak, but one that is too **large** is wrong, and it becomes too large the moment
any single constraint is not valid. It checks LP-min ≤ truth ≤ LP-max on fifteen
configurations whose size is known independently — from four lattices and three separate
sources of truth. If any constraint were too strong, some truth would fall below its own
minimum. None does. `capalgebra.py` re-derives the cap construction's seven inequalities and
its count in exact rational arithmetic, independently of every script that uses them, and
reproduces Cohn's table in dimensions 26, 28–31 from the count alone.

No floating-point arithmetic decides anything. Every linear-programming bound carries an
exact rational dual certificate, so an imprecise solver can only produce a *weaker* bound,
never an invalid one. Every Gram matrix used is proved realizable — a bound for a Gram that
does not occur is worth nothing, and dimension 69 was withdrawn once on exactly this ground
before the triple was exhibited in coordinates. Every construction is verified in explicit coordinates
where the configuration is small enough to write down, and by exact integer arithmetic on the
Gram where it is not, with outstanding certificate gaps identified explicitly.
Published comparisons are dated: **Cohn's table moves**, and two entries (dimensions
12 and 19) changed while this work was in progress. The supersession table above records
the later September publication separately from the pinned computational baselines.

Negative results are recorded as carefully as positive ones, in
`[verifications/closed/](verifications/closed/)`, because they are what stops the next
attempt from wasting time. Among them: dimensions 17–24 are a single construction, the layer
identity τ(Λ₁₆₊ₖ) = 4320 + 513·N₂(Lₖ) + 32·N₄(Lₖ), verified as a structure inside the Leech
lattice and with every component at a stated ceiling but one; the Cohn–Li mechanism has
method-specific ceilings in dimensions 19–21; Λ₂₁, Λ₂₂ and Λ₂₃ have exact min-max cosines
√(8/29), √(3/11), √(4/15); the antipode construction is a max-weight clique problem whose
arms lie in a 30° cap, which caps it structurally; and the maximum-class problem survives
every two-point method, the three-point SDP and the subconstituent split at 4680/11 = 425.45.

`common/checkpoint.py` checks complete integrity manifests and runs the new
source verifiers in temporary copies. `source/dim61_96/verify_support_bits.py`

- **Re-fetch the published table before claiming anything.** It moved twice during this work
(dimensions 12 and 19), and the range above dimension 48 — where no table has entries at
all — is the easiest place to be wrong about what "previously known" means.
- **Test new LP code on a pair of equivalent Gram matrices.** (3,−3,0) and 3·A₃ must give the
same answer. A missing-moments bug hid behind that for a day.
